title_zh: 阴茎癌的致癌机制:HPV、炎症和其他途径
source_body_en: Objective: Penile cancer, though rare, carries profound clinical and psychosocial consequences. Its diagnosis often occurs at advanced stages, leading to mutilating surgeries and severe impairment in quality of life. Approximately 95% of penile malignancies are squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs), with a global 5-year cancer-specific survival rate of ~65%. Recent advances have shifted attention from purely oncologic outcomes toward understanding its molecular heterogeneity and etiopathogenesis. Growing evidence supports a dual carcinogenic model involving viral and non-viral pathways, driven respectively by human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and chronic inflammatory dermatoses. The objectives of the study are to synthesize current evidence on the molecular, immunologic, and epigenetic mechanisms underlying HPV-related and HPV-independent penile SCC, emphasizing their epidemiologic relevance, pathogenic interplay, and clinical implications. Materials and Methods: A critical appraisal of epidemiological, molecular, and immunological studies was conducted, and evidence was graded according to the Oxford classification for levels of evidence and strength of recommendation. Systematic searches were conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Literatura Latino-Americana e do Caribe em Ciências da Saúde, covering publications from January 2000 to October 2025. Search terms included (“penile cancer” OR “penile carcinoma” OR “penile squamous cell carcinoma” OR “cancer of the penis”) AND (“HPV” OR “human papillomavirus” OR “lichen sclerosus” OR “balanitis” OR “chronic inflammation” OR “carcinogenesis” OR “molecular mechanism” OR “tumor microenvironment” OR “epigenetics” OR “non-coding RNA” OR “APOBEC” OR “immune checkpoint” OR “p16” OR “TP53” OR “E6 oncoprotein” OR “E7 oncoprotein” OR “p16INK4a” OR “viral integration” OR “HPV DNA” OR “E6/E7 mRNA” OR “pRb inactivation” OR “p53 degradation” OR “CDKN2A methylation” OR “DNA methylation” OR “histone modification” OR “miRNA” OR “lncRNA” OR “piRNA” OR “cancer-associated fibroblast” OR “tumor-associated macrophage” OR “immune checkpoint” OR “PD-L1” OR “EBV” OR “HSV” OR “viral co-infection”). Studies were selected according to predefined inclusion criteria (systematic reviews, clinical trials, and cohort studies with histological confirmation) and exclusion criteria (case reports, series with Results: Two distinct but occasionally overlapping oncogenic mechanisms drive penile carcinogenesis. The HPV-related pathway, responsible for 30–50% of cases, is predominantly associated with HPV-16 and HPV-18. Viral oncoproteins E6 and E7 promote p53 degradation and retinoblastoma (pRb) inactivation, resulting in uncontrolled proliferation and p16^INK4a^ overexpression. Integration of viral DNA into the host genome disrupts regulatory genes and induces epigenetic alterations, including hypermethylation of CDKN2A and global hypomethylation. HPV-positive tumors typically exhibit lower mutational burden, higher immune infiltration, and improved prognosis. Nonetheless, HPV-driven lesions display enrichment of immunosuppressive cells (FoxP3+ regulatory T cells and CD163+ macrophages), and upregulation of immune checkpoints (programmed cell death 1, lymphocyte activation gene-3, T cell immunoglobulin and mucin-domain containing-3), favoring immune exhaustion and tumor persistence. Conversely, the HPV-independent pathway arises primarily from chronic inflammatory and dermatologic conditions such as lichen sclerosus and balanitis. Persistent inflammation generates oxidative stress and DNA damage, driving tumor protein 53 (TP53) mutations and activating nuclear factor kappa B, cyclooxygenase-2, interleukin 6/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3, and transforming growth factor-beta signaling cascades. These molecular events establish a tumor-promoting microenvironment characterized by angiogenesis, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and immune evasion. Genetic susceptibility through polymorphisms in DNA repair (TP53, breast cancer gene 2, excision repair cross-complementing 4) and immune-regulatory genes modulates individual risk. In addition, dysregulation of non-coding RNAs (miR-21, miR-223, miR-744-5p), APOBEC3-mediated mutagenesis, and viral co-infections (herpes simplex virus, Epstein-Barr virus) contribute to genomic instability and disease progression. Conclusion: Penile carcinogenesis represents a multifactorial process involving viral, inflammatory, and host-genetic interactions that converge on immune evasion and genomic instability. HPV-driven and inflammation-mediated pathways may act synergistically, amplifying oncogenic potential through shared inflammatory and epigenetic circuits. Integration of HPV testing, p16 immunohistochemistry, and molecular profiling into clinical practice is instrumental for accurate classification, prognostic refinement, and the development of precision-based prevention and treatment strategies. Public health efforts focused on HPV vaccination, early circumcision, and management of chronic inflammatory conditions remain critical to reducing incidence and mortality, particularly in high-burden regions such as Latin America and sub-Saharan Africa.
abstract_zh: 目的:阴茎癌虽然罕见,但会带来深远的临床和社会心理后果。其 诊断 通常发生在晚期,导致残肢手术和生活质量严重受损。大约 95% 的阴茎恶性肿瘤是鳞状细胞癌 (SCC),全球癌症特异性 5 年生存率约为 65%。最近的进展已将注意力从纯粹的肿瘤学结果转向了解其分子异质性和发病机制。越来越多的证据支持涉及病毒和非病毒途径的双重致癌模型,分别由 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染和慢性炎症性皮肤病驱动。该研究的目的是综合有关 HPV 相关和 HPV 独立阴茎 SCC 的分子、免疫学和表观遗传机制的最新证据,强调它们的流行病学相关性、致病相互作用和临床意义。材料和方法:对流行病学、分子和免疫学研究进行严格评估,并根据牛津分类的证据级别和推荐强度对证据进行分级。在 PubMed/MEDLINE、Scopus、Web of Science 和 Literatura Latino-Americana e do Caribe em Ciências da Saúde 中进行了系统检索,涵盖 2000 年 1 月至 2025 年 10 月的出版物。检索词包括(“阴茎癌”或“阴茎癌”或“阴茎鳞状细胞癌”或“阴茎癌”)AND(“HPV”或“人乳头瘤病毒”或“硬化性苔藓”或“龟头炎”或“慢性炎症”或“癌变”或“分子机制”或“肿瘤微环境”或“表观遗传学”或“非编码RNA”或“APOBEC”或“免疫检查点”或“p16”或“TP53”或“E6癌蛋白”或“E7癌蛋白”或“p16INK4a”或“病毒整合”或“HPV DNA”或“E6/E7 mRNA”或“pRb失活”或“p53降解”或“CDKN2A甲基化”或“DNA甲基化”或“组蛋白修饰”或“miRNA”或“lncRNA”或“piRNA”或“癌症相关成纤维细胞”或“肿瘤相关巨噬细胞”或“免疫检查点”或“PD-L1”或“EBV”或“HSV”或“病毒”共同感染”)。根据预先确定的纳入标准(系统评价、临床试验和具有组织学确认的 队列研究 研究)和排除标准(病例报告,结果系列:两种不同但偶尔重叠的致癌机制驱动阴茎癌)选择研究。HPV 相关途径导致 30-50% 的病例,主要与 HPV-16 和 HPV-18 相关。病毒癌蛋白 E6 和 E7 促进 p53 降解和视网膜母细胞瘤 (pRb) 失活,导致增殖失控和 p16^INK4a^ 过度表达。病毒 DNA 整合到 宿主 基因组 中会破坏调节基因并诱导表观遗传改变,包括 CDKN2A 的高甲基化和整体低甲基化。HPV 阳性肿瘤通常表现出较低的突变负担、较高的免疫浸润和改善的预后。尽管如此,HPV 驱动的病变显示出免疫抑制细胞(FoxP3+ 调节性 T 细胞和 CD163+ 巨噬细胞)的富集,以及免疫检查点(程序性细胞死亡 1、淋巴细胞激活基因 3、T 细胞免疫球蛋白和粘蛋白结构域 3)的上调,有利于免疫耗竭和肿瘤持续存在。相反,HPV 独立途径主要源于慢性炎症和皮肤病,例如硬化性苔藓和龟头炎。持续的炎症会产生氧化应激和 DNA 损伤,驱动肿瘤蛋白 53 (TP53) 突变 并激活核因子 kappa B、环氧合酶-2、白细胞介素 6/信号转导器和转录激活剂 3,以及转化生长因子-β 信号级联。这些分子事件建立了一个以血管生成、上皮间质转化和免疫逃避为特征的肿瘤促进微环境。遗传易感性通过 DNA 修复(TP53、乳腺癌基因 2、切除修复交叉互补 4)和免疫调节基因的多态性调节个体风险。此外,非编码RNA(miR-21、miR-223、miR-744-5p)的失调、APOBEC3介导的诱变和病毒联合感染(单纯疱疹病毒、Epstein-Barr病毒)会导致基因组不稳定和疾病进展。结论:阴茎癌发生是一个多因素过程,涉及病毒、炎症和 宿主 基因相互作用,这些相互作用集中在免疫逃避和基因组不稳定上。HPV 驱动的通路和炎症介导的通路可能协同作用,通过共享的炎症和表观遗传回路放大致癌潜力。将 HPV 检测、p16 免疫组织化学和分子分析整合到临床实践中,有助于准确分类、完善预后以及制定精准预防和 治疗 策略。专注于 HPV 疫苗接种、早期包皮环切和慢性炎症管理的公共卫生工作对于减少 发病率 和 死亡率 仍然至关重要,特别是在拉丁美洲和撒哈拉以南非洲等高负担地区。

title: How Would You Screen This 26-Year-Old Woman for Cervical Cancer? Grand Rounds Discussion From Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center.
abstract: Cervical cancer is the third most common gynecologic cancer, with more than 13 000 new cases diagnosed in 2025. The incidence of and mortality from cervical cancer vary across racial and ethnic groups and in persons living in medically underserved or geographically isolated areas, with half of all cervical cancers occurring in women who are underscreened or have never been screened. Persistent infection with high-risk types of human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most important risk factor for cervical cancer and is associated with nearly all cases. Although genital tract HPV infection is common, most HPV infections are transient, and cervical cancer occurs in only a small portion of patients with HPV. For decades, cervical cancer screening relied on annual cytologic assessment. A growing understanding of the role of HPV infection in the natural progression of cervical cancer has led to updated screening recommendations from the American Cancer Society and the Women's Preventive Services Initiative, as well as a draft update from the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force. These recommendations include primary HPV testing as a preferred screening strategy and include an option for self-collected specimens for HPV testing. Here, 2 experts in this field, a primary care physician and an obstetrics and gynecology physician, debate how to apply these guidelines when screening a patient for cervical cancer. They discuss a range of screening options and consider the challenges of applying these guidelines across different age groups and in patients at increased risk.

title: HPV co-infection burden, vaginal microbiota restructuring, and host context are associated with Cervical precancer risk in a racially restricted observational cohort
abstract: Abstract Background High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is necessary for cervical carcinogenesis, but HPV detection alone does not distinguish transient infection from lesions at greatest risk of progression. We evaluated whether HPV burden, vaginal microbiota structure, and host-context variables jointly characterize cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN3) in a Black/African American and White analytic cohort from the Vaginal Microbiome Health Project (VaMHP), integrating L1-based HPV typing, 16S rRNA vaginal microbiota profiling, and linked clinical metadata. Results Among 1181 participants, 75 had CIN3. CIN3 was associated with HPV positivity (55/75, 73.3% vs 431/1106, 39.0%; odds ratio [OR] 4.31, 95% CI 2.55–7.29; Fisher exact p = 7.9 x 10^-9) and with multiple HPV infection among HPV-positive participants (35/55, 63.6% vs 176/431, 40.8%; OR 2.54, 95% CI 1.42–4.54; p = 0.0022). HPV communities in CIN3-positive samples showed higher Shannon diversity, greater observed strain richness, higher evenness, and significant beta-diversity separation. In vaginal microbiota analyses, alpha diversity did not differ by CIN3 status, but community composition did, and Lactobacillus crispatus was the only taxon depleted in CIN3 after multiple-testing correction. Race, age, and metronidazole exposure were central nodes in the host-factor network. In predictive modeling, a full integrated model combining metadata, HPV, and vaginal microbiota features (auROC = 0.745) outperformed both HPV + vaginal microbiota (auROC = 0.670) and HPV-only (auROC = 0.440) models. Conclusions CIN3 in this cohort was associated with coordinated shifts in virologic burden, vaginal community structure, and host social-clinical context. The results support a structure-function interpretation in which loss of Lactobacillus crispatus-dominant states and enrichment of dysbiosis-associated communities define a host-microbiome context that is more permissive to HPV persistence and precancer. These findings move beyond descriptive omics by showing that microbiome and host-context features add nonredundant discriminatory signal beyond HPV-only models.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between HPV co-infection, vaginal microbiota restructuring, and host context with cervical precancer risk in a racially restricted observational cohort. The research highlights that HPV burden, microbiota composition, and host factors jointly contribute to the risk of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN3). The findings show that CIN3-positive samples have distinct microbial profiles, including higher diversity and depletion of Lactobacillus crispatus. The study also demonstrates that integrating microbiota and host data improves predictive modeling for CIN3 compared to HPV-only models. These results suggest that host-microbiome interactions may influence HPV persistence and precancer development, offering insights into potential surveillance and prevention strategies. However, the evidence is based on an abstract-only review, and specific limitations of the study design are not detailed.

title: Altered immune responses in HR-HPV infected women
abstract: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) is the primary cause of cervical cancer (CC). However, most HPV infections are transient and are cleared by effective host immune responses. Therefore, understanding the mechanisms that allow viral persistence and immune escape is critical to explaining why only a subset of women develops cervical lesions and invasive cancer. Although cervical cancer is largely preventable through vaccination and screening, it remains a major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality among women worldwide, with a disproportionate burden in low- and middle-income countries. This significant disparity underscores the ongoing inequities in access to HPV vaccination, screening, and timely treatment, which hinder the World Health Organization aim to eliminate cervical cancer as a public health concern by 2030. This narrative review examines how viral, host, and microenvironmental factors interact to promote HR-HPV persistence and cervical cancer development, with particular attention to evidence from Mexican women. HR-HPV can evade immune surveillance by interfering with innate immune recognition, interferon signaling, antigen presentation, and cytotoxic lymphocyte activity. These alterations are compounded by cervicovaginal dysbiosis, immunosuppressive cytokines, regulatory-cell expansion, host genetic variation, and altered microRNA expression. Together, these interconnected processes impair viral clearance and create conditions that favor the progression of cervical lesions to invasive cancer. A comprehensive understanding of these mechanisms may facilitate the identification of biomarkers of HPV persistence and disease progression, while supporting the development of more effective immunotherapeutic strategies and precision prevention approaches, particularly for populations disproportionately affected by cervical cancer.

title: CDK4/6 inhibition radiosensitizes p16-negative squamous cell carcinomas of the aerodigestive tract via cell cycle arrest.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: CDK4/6 inhibitors have quickly entered clinical guidelines for luminal breast cancer, but their role in other cancer types remains to be defined. Squamous cell carcinomas not driven by human papillomavirus (HPV-negative SCCs) are frequently treated with radiotherapy, and concurrent treatment with CDK4/6 inhibitors has been proposed. We sought to investigate the efficacy of this combination across a range of HPV-negative SCCs and define molecular biomarkers of response that could be used for treatment selection. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We employed clonogenic assays and a previously described long-term viability assay for measuring radiation response to identify radioresistant cells within HPV-negative SCC cell lines. Among consistently radioresistant lines, we conducted drug/radiation combinations to measure additive effects of the CDK4/6 inhibitors, abemaciclib and palbociclib. Mechanistic effects of drug/radiation combinations were further investigated by flow cytometry, immunocytochemistry, and western blot. Efficacy was validated in vivo using an HPV-negative SCC cell line xenograft. RESULTS: Among the 19 HPV-negative SCC cell lines, 6 were consistently radioresistant using both clonogenic and viability assays. We validated the use of the viability assay for drug/radiation combinations using known radiosensitizing drug, cisplatin, before applying it to the CDK4/6 inhibitors. Five of the 6 radioresistant cell lines displayed a favorable combination effect with both CDK4/6 inhibitors. Sensitivity to the combination was reliant on drug-induced cell cycle arrest and correlated with lack of p16 activity in the presence of Rb. Combining abemaciclib with radiation reduced tumor growth in xenografted mice. CONCLUSIONS: CDK4/6 inhibitors are good candidates for further preclinical and clinical evaluation in combination with radiation in HPV-negative SCCs due to their effects on cell cycle phase in cells with Rb protein activity and low p16 levels. The long-term viability assay allows for efficient testing of drug/radiation combinations and can be considered for future experiments as part of a bench-to-bedside translational pipeline.

title: Factors associated with cytology triage attendance after a hrHPV-positive self-sample and age-related differences: The lifelines cohort.
abstract: BackgroundSelf-sampling for high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing has been introduced in cervical cancer screening programs to improve participation. In the Netherlands, women with an hrHPV-positive self-sample are required to visit their GP's office for cytology triage, as this cannot be performed on self-sampled material. Non-attendance at this step reduces screening effectiveness. This study examined whether sociodemographic and health-related behavioural factors commonly associated with screening participation are also associated with cytology triage attendance after an hrHPV-positive self-sample and whether these associations differ by age.MethodsWe conducted a study on the Lifelines cohort of participants in the Dutch cervical cancer screening program who used self-sampling between 2017 and 2024. The main outcome was cytology triage attendance within 6 months after an hrHPV-positive self-sample. Lifelines contains data on sociodemographic and behavioural factors including education, income, marital status, smoking, alcohol, diet, body mass index, physical activity, television viewing, sleep duration, lifetime use of hormonal contraception, parity, number of children and age at first childbirth. Logistic regression analyses were performed, including age-stratified models.ResultsAmong women with an hrHPV-positive self-sample, 10.2% did not attend cytology triage within 6 months. Most sociodemographic and lifestyle factors were not associated with cytology triage attendance, and no meaningful differences were observed between age groups. However, inadequate prior screening history was associated with lower odds of cytology triage attendance.ConclusionsThe lack of associations with lifestyle or sociodemographic factors suggest that program-level strategies such as how hrHPV test results are communicated, might be more effective in increasing triage participation than interventions targeting specific subgroups.

title: Cellular senescence and immortalization technologies in translational medicine: from fundamental mechanisms to therapeutic platforms
abstract: Primary cell cultures are an indispensable tool in fundamental research within modern cell biology. Their value lies in their close physiological resemblance to in vivo conditions, which significantly enhances the reliability and translational relevance of experimental data. However, the broad application of primary cells in vitro is constrained by their finite proliferative capacity, culminating in cellular senescence, which poses substantial challenges for long-term and highly reproducible studies. Cellular senescence represents a complex, multifaceted cellular response to diverse stimuli. Consequently, it is broadly classified into replicative senescence, oncogene-induced senescence (OIS), and stress-induced premature senescence. Each of these senescence modalities exhibits distinct molecular signatures, and elucidating these features is crucial for understanding how to bypass the cellular proliferative barrier through immortalization. Classical immortalization strategies, such as the ectopic expression of the telomerase catalytic subunit (TERT) or the introduction of viral oncogenes (e.g., SV40 Large T-antigen, HPV16 E6/E7) and proto-oncogenes, are highly effective but carry significant limitations. These include the inherent risk of oncogenic transformation and the alteration of the native cellular phenotype. Consequently, contemporary approaches such as conditional immortalization, non-integrating delivery systems, and combinatorial strategies are gaining prominence. These methods aim to sustain a high proliferative potential while preserving maximal phenotypic fidelity to the original primary cells. This review systematizes current knowledge regarding the distinct modalities of cellular senescence. It provides a comprehensive analysis of both primary and auxiliary immortalization techniques, critically evaluating their respective advantages and limitations. Furthermore, it characterizes contemporary immortalized cell lines with a specific focus on their phenotypic stability and translational potential in regenerative medicine, tissue engineering, 3D cell culture models, and preclinical pharmacology. The analysis presented herein is primarily based on data published within the last 15 years.

title: Intersectional inequalities in HPV vaccination among female college students in China: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is central to the World Health Organization strategy for cervical cancer elimination. China introduced free two-dose bivalent HPV vaccination for eligible 13-year-old girls in November 2025. We estimated inequalities in self-reported receipt of any HPV vaccine among female college students immediately before this national programme. Methods We analysed 44,052 female respondents from the 2025 National College Student Survey on Sexual and Reproductive Health (NCSS-SRH), a large weighted multi-institutional online survey conducted from April to September 2025 across all 31 mainland provincial-level administrative units. Modified Poisson models estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs), with standard errors clustered by current institution. title: HPV Vaccination Uptake Among Vaccine-Eligible U.S. Adults with and Without a Cancer History: A National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey Analysis, 2011–2023
abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus includes more than 200 types, classified by cancer risk. Since 2006, the vaccine has effectively prevented human papillomavirus infection and associated cancers; however, coverage among adults remains low. Furthermore, research examining human papillomavirus vaccination among adults with a cancer history is limited. Objective: To estimate vaccination uptake for human papillomavirus among U.S. adults aged 20–47 and compare uptake by cancer history. Methods: This study used data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey from 2011 to 2023. The final analytic sample included 13,511 adults aged 20–47 with self-reported vaccination status and cancer history. The data were weighted to account for the complex survey design and produce nationally representative estimates. Results: Among eligible adults, 84.7% were unvaccinated, 2.9% were under-vaccinated, and 12.4% had completed the vaccine series. Among eligible adults with a self-reported cancer history, the majority were unvaccinated. Vaccination completion differed by sociodemographic and healthcare-related factors. Conclusions: Human papillomavirus vaccination remained low among eligible U.S. adults, including those with a self-reported cancer history. These findings support efforts to improve adult vaccination coverage and prevent human papillomavirus infections and associated cancers.

title: Anal Cancer: A Multidisciplinary Management
abstract: Anal squamous cell carcinoma (ASCC) is an uncommon malignancy accounting for a small proportion of gastrointestinal cancers; however, its incidence has progressively increased worldwide, particularly among individuals with persistent high-risk human papillomavirus infection and immunosuppression. Historically, treatment was based on radical surgery with abdominoperineal resection (APR), resulting in permanent colostomy and significant morbidity. The introduction of definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) has radically changed the therapeutic approach, establishing organ preservation as the primary goal of treatment. Definitive CRT based on fluoropyrimidine and mitomycin C remains the standard treatment for localized ASCC, achieving complete clinical response in the majority of patients and avoiding radical surgery in most cases. Surgery currently plays a selective but essential role. Local excision may be considered in carefully selected superficial T1 lesions, whereas APR remains the standard salvage procedure for persistent or recurrent disease after CRT when complete resection is feasible. Salvage surgery is technically challenging because of previous irradiation, fibrosis, altered anatomy, and increased risk of wound complications; however, achievement of an R0 resection remains the strongest predictor of long-term survival. Emerging strategies, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, therapeutic HPV vaccines, molecularly targeted therapies, and circulating tumor HPV DNA monitoring, may further modify future treatment algorithms. The management of ASCC has evolved from routine radical surgery to a multidisciplinary, organ-preserving approach. Optimal outcomes depend on accurate staging, careful patient selection, and management within experienced multidisciplinary teams. Future integration of molecular biomarkers and immunotherapy may further refine the role of surgery and contribute to more personalized treatment strategies.

title: HPV vaccination coverage and barriers for people with disability: A scoping review
abstract: This scoping review explored human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination coverage and barriers for people with disability. Our global search identified 33 studies, all from high-income countries, published between 2006 and 2025. We found evidence of inequalities in HPV vaccination coverage for people with disability across a range of countries, sexes/genders, settings, and disability groups. Common vaccination barriers included misassumptions around sexual activity, lack of vaccination recommendations from healthcare professionals in primarily healthcare-facility-based HPV vaccination programme settings, and lack of staff training/resources. There were marked gaps in population-wide research for all people with disability, research from low- and middle-income settings, and research including deaf or blind communities, or people with physical or psychosocial disability. Disability-inclusive research methodologies were limited and should be prioritized to ensure future research meets community needs. If HPV vaccination targets are to be achieved, equitable access must be supported for all people, including people with disability.

abstract_zh: 本次范围界定审查探讨了 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗接种 的覆盖范围和残疾人士面临的障碍。我们的全球检索确定了 2006 年至 2025 年间发表的 33 项研究,全部来自高收入国家。我们发现了不同国家、不同性别、不同环境和不同残疾群体的残疾人 HPV 疫苗接种 覆盖率不平等的证据。常见的 疫苗接种 障碍包括对性活动的误解、在主要基于医疗机构的 HPV 疫苗接种 计划设置中缺乏医疗保健专业人员的 疫苗接种 建议以及缺乏员工培训/资源。针对所有残疾人的全人口研究、低收入和中等收入环境的研究以及包括聋哑人或盲人社区或有身体或心理残疾的人的研究都存在明显差距。包容残疾人的研究方法有限,应优先考虑以确保未来的研究满足社区需求。如果要实现 HPV 疫苗接种 目标,必须支持所有人(包括残疾人)公平获得疫苗。

title: DA PROFILAXIA À TERAPÊUTICA: UMA REVISÃO INTEGRATIVA SOBRE AS INOVAÇÕES NANOTECNOLÓGICAS E IMUNOLÓGICAS NO MANEJO DO HPV. FROM PROPHYLAXIS TO THERAPEUTICS: AN INTEGRATIVE REVIEW OF NANOTECHNOLOGICAL AND IMMUNOLOGICAL INNOVATIONS IN HPV MANAGEMENT
abstract: Objetivo: Analisar as evidências científicas acerca das inovações nanotecnológicas e imunológicas aplicadas ao manejo do Papilomavírus Humano (HPV), com ênfase no desenvolvimento de vacinas terapêuticas, sistemas nanoestruturados de liberação e ferramentas de apoio ao diagnóstico. Métodos: Revisão integrativa da literatura, conduzida nas bases de dados MEDLINE/PubMed, LILACS e BDENF, utilizando os descritores Papillomaviridae, Papillomavirus Vaccines, Nanotechnology, Drug Delivery Systems e Immunotherapy, combinados pelos operadores booleanos AND e OR. Foram incluídos estudos publicados entre 2016 e 2026, nos idiomas português, inglês e espanhol, que abordassem estratégias nanotecnológicas e imunológicas para o manejo do HPV. Após as etapas de identificação, triagem e elegibilidade, 11 estudos compuseram a amostra final. Resultados: As evidências foram organizadas em três eixos temáticos: avanços nanotecnológicos aplicados ao manejo do HPV, inovações imunológicas e desenvolvimento de vacinas terapêuticas, e biotecnologia molecular associada à inteligência artificial. Os estudos demonstraram que sistemas nanoestruturados favorecem a liberação controlada de imunobiológicos e fármacos, enquanto vacinas terapêuticas direcionadas às oncoproteínas E6 e E7 potencializam a resposta imune celular contra células infectadas. Além disso, ferramentas de inteligência artificial e biomarcadores moleculares ampliam a precisão do rastreamento e do diagnóstico precoce. Conclusão: As tecnologias emergentes analisadas apresentam elevado potencial para transformar o manejo das infecções persistentes pelo HPV, favorecendo abordagens diagnósticas e terapêuticas mais precisas, conservadoras e individualizadas. Apesar dos resultados promissores, sua ampla incorporação à prática clínica depende da realização de estudos multicêntricos, validação clínica e avaliação de custo-efetividade, contribuindo para o fortalecimento das estratégias de prevenção e controle do câncer do colo do útero.

title: Systems Pharmacology of Human Oncoviruses: Network-Based Drug Discovery for Virus-Driven Cancers.
abstract: Human oncoviruses, including high-risk HPV, EBV, HBV, HCV, MCPyV, KSHV, and HTLV-1, account for approximately 15%-20% of global human malignancies. Rather than acting through isolated pathways, viral oncoproteins systematically rewire host regulatory networks, rendering conventional single-target oncology paradigms vulnerable to rapid resistance and clinical failure. Systems pharmacology offers a transformative, network-centric framework that views virus-driven cancers as systemic perturbations of host protein-protein interaction networks. This review synthesises computational methodology, network topology, and drug discovery strategies across major human oncoviruses. We examine how graph centrality algorithms, quantitative network proximity metrics (Z-score), and complementary exposure synergy modelling (SAB) uncover hidden network vulnerabilities and guide targeted drug repurposing. Despite distinct genomic structures and tissue tropisms, oncogenic viruses converge on shared host interactome hubs, notably TP53, AKT1, BCL2, MYC, STAT3, and VEGFA, to drive cell cycle dysregulation, apoptotic suppression, and microenvironmental remodelling. We evaluate repositioned synthetic pharmaceuticals (such as kinase inhibitors and host ion channel blockers) and multi-target bioactive formulations, detailing their mechanisms in targeting viral host dependencies. Finally, we address key translational bottlenecks, including disparities between in silico binding predictions and in vivo pharmacokinetics, extensive plasma protein binding, tumour penetration barriers, and viral latency reservoirs. Overcoming these hurdles will require integrating deep graph learning, single-cell spatial multi-omics, and patient-derived organoid models to accelerate the clinical realization of network-targeted therapies in viral oncology.

title: VACINAÇÃO CONTRA O HPV: ATUALIZAÇÃO DAS ESTRATÉGIAS DE IMUNIZAÇÃO NO BRASIL E SUA RELEVÂNCIA PARA A SAÚDE DA MULHER
abstract: Introdução: A infecção pelo papilomavírus humano (HPV) é a infecção sexualmente transmissível mais prevalente no mundo e constitui o principal fator de risco para o desenvolvimento do câncer do colo do útero, além de estar associada a neoplasias de vulva, vagina, ânus e orofaringe1. A vacinação representa a principal estratégia de prevenção primária dessas doenças1. Nos últimos anos, recomendações internacionais e políticas públicas brasileiras vêm atualizando as estratégias de imunização, buscando ampliar a cobertura vacinal e reduzir a incidência do câncer do colo do útero como problema de saúde pública2.Objetivo: Revisar a literatura disponível acerca das recentes atualizações das estratégias de vacinação contra o HPV no Brasil e suas implicações para a promoção da saúde da mulher.Metodologia: Trata-se de uma revisão da literatura de caráter descritivo. Foram realizadas buscas na base de dados PubMed, utilizando os descritores “HPV vaccination” e “Human papillomavirus”. Também foram consultados documentos oficiais do Ministério da Saúde e da Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS). Foram incluídos estudos em português e inglês, no período de 2020 a 2026, que abordassem estratégias de imunização, efetividade vacinal, cobertura vacinal e políticas públicas relacionadas ao HPV.Resultados: A literatura demonstra elevada efetividade da vacinação contra o HPV na prevenção de infecções persistentes pelos subtipos oncogênicos, reduzindo significativamente a incidência de lesões precursoras e do câncer do colo do útero3. Além da proteção individual, a vacinação contribui para o desenvolvimento da imunidade coletiva ao reduzir a circulação viral, a transmissão do HPV e, consequentemente, a prevalência da infecção na população3. Entre as principais atualizações recentes destacam-se a adoção do esquema de dose única para indivíduos imunocompetentes na faixa etária recomendada e, no contexto brasileiro, a prorrogação da estratégia de resgate vacinal até 31 de dezembro de 2026, destinada a adolescentes e jovens de 15 a 19 anos que não receberam a vacina na idade preconizada2. Essa medida busca ampliar a cobertura vacinal, reduzir o número de indivíduos suscetíveis à infecção e aproximar o país das metas propostas pela Organização Mundial da Saúde para eliminação do câncer do colo do útero4. Entretanto, estudos apontam que a hesitação vacinal, as desigualdades regionais e as dificuldades de acesso aos serviços de saúde permanecem como importantes obstáculos para o sucesso dessas estratégias5.Conclusão: As recentes atualizações das estratégias de vacinação contra o HPV fortalecem as ações de prevenção do câncer do colo do útero e representam importante avanço para a saúde pública brasileira1,2. A ampliação das oportunidades de imunização, especialmente por meio da estratégia de resgate para jovens não vacinados, tem potencial para aumentar a cobertura vacinal e reduzir a carga das doenças relacionadas ao HPV2. Contudo, a efetividade dessas medidas depende da continuidade das campanhas educativas, da qualificação dos serviços de saúde e da adesão da população às estratégias de vacinação3.

title: Decoding the Connection: Cervicovaginal Microbiome, HPV, and Cervical Cancer
abstract: In low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where access to screenings and preventative care is restricted, cervical cancer continues to pose a serious threat to world health. In these areas, it is the third most prevalent cancer among women, and increased incidence and mortality are a result of resource inequities. The human papillomavirus (HPV), a sexually transmitted infection, is the main cause of cervical cancer. Nonetheless, studies reveal a complex interplay among environmental, genetic, and epigenetic factors, with mounting evidence supporting the role of the cervicovaginal microbiome. This microbial community controls vaginal health and modulates HPV risks, with some bacterial species, such as those linked to bacterial vaginosis (e.g., Lactobacillus iners), potentially promoting HPV persistence and cervical dysplasia. On the other hand, beneficial species, including Lactobacillus crispatus and Lactobacillus gasseri, contribute to an acidic environment that counters inflammation and may limit HPV progression. Although progress has been made in understanding these dynamics, much remains unknown about the factors influencing microbiome variability and how to manipulate it to prevent disease. Meanwhile, established preventive measures, such as HPV vaccination, routine screenings, and early treatment of precancerous lesions, have proven effective. However, logistical and financial challenges in LMICs hinder broader implementation. To reduce the global burden, efforts must focus on affordable vaccines, integrated screening services, and increasing public awareness. Further microbiome research offers hope for innovative prevention and treatments. Addressing systemic barriers and advancing knowledge could signify meaningful steps toward eradicating cervical cancer as a public health threat worldwide.

title: Association between breast cancer and nipple suction as a sexual practice in Women from Northern Mexico.
abstract: Infectious agents may play a role in breast cancer. Viral sequences of Epstein–Barr virus, human papillomavirus, and murine mammary tumor virus have been identified in breast tumors. A potential but unexplored pathway for viral entry is nipple suction during sexual practices. We aimed to evaluate the association between nipple suction as a sexual practice and breast cancer in women. We conducted a secondary analysis of a large population-based case-control study carried out between 2007 and 2011 in five northern Mexican states. The sample included 988 women with histologically confirmed incident breast cancer and 1019 matched controls without the disease. Information was obtained through standardized face-to-face interviews. Nipple suction was assessed via self-report, with responses categorized as never, sometimes, or frequently/always. We used logistic regression to estimate the association between breast cancer and nipple suction, adjusting for age and breastfeeding duration, with stratified analyses by menopausal status and tumor immunophenotype. Nipple suction was positively associated with breast cancer, with a significant dose-response trend ( P < 0.001). Compared with never, women reporting occasional suction had higher odds [odds ratio (OR) = 1.38, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.14–1.67], and those reporting frequent/always showed a markedly increased risk (OR = 14.36, 95% CI: 9.22–22.35). Associations were consistent across menopausal groups and tumor subtypes. Our findings raise the hypothesis that nipple suction could represent a potential route of exposure to oncogenic viruses present in saliva; however, molecular and virological studies are warranted to evaluate this possible mechanism.

title: A randomized, placebo-controlled, phase II study of docetaxel and platinum with or without erlotinib in recurrent/metastatic head and neck squamous-cell carcinomas.
abstract: PURPOSE: We conducted a randomized phase II trial to evaluate whether adding erlotinib to platinum/docetaxel improves clinical outcomes in the first-line treatment of recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous-cell carcinomas, building on our previous single-arm phase II trial. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This was a placebo-controlled, double-blind, single-center phase II study. Patients (N = 120) were randomly assigned (1 : 1) to receive platinum (carboplatin area under the curve 6 or cisplatin 75 mg/m2 every 21 days for six cycles) plus docetaxel (75 mg/m2 every 21 days for six cycles) with either erlotinib (150 mg/day orally until progression) or placebo. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints included overall survival, response rates, duration of response, and correlations of erlotinib-induced rash/biomarkers with outcomes. RESULTS: Median PFS was 6.1 months with erlotinib versus 4.4 months with placebo [hazard ratio (HR) 0.63, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.42-0.95, P = 0.026]. Median overall survival was 17.0 months in the erlotinib arm compared with 13.7 months in the control arm (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.43-1.04, P = 0.0718), meeting the prespecified type I error threshold. Subgroup analyses demonstrated numerically favorable PFS HRs across most clinical subgroups, with a more pronounced benefit observed in patients with oropharyngeal and human papillomavirus-related tumors. Development of grade ≥2 rash during the first cycle of erlotinib was associated with significantly improved overall survival (HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.19-0.87, P = 0.021). The addition of erlotinib increased the incidence of grade 2-4 adverse events, particularly gastrointestinal toxicity, rash, fatigue, and dehydration but no unexpected safety signals were observed. CONCLUSIONS: The study met its primary endpoint, supporting the continued relevance of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) inhibition in this disease. Although contemporary immunotherapy-based standards limit direct adoption of this regimen, these results provide clinically meaningful insight into EGFR biology and support further development of modernized, tyrosine kinase inhibitor-based EGFR strategies, including rational combinations and biomarker-driven approaches, to improve outcomes.

title: EVIDENCE AND RECOMMENDATIONS ON THE USE OF THE HPV DNA MOLECULAR TEST AS A CERVICAL CANCER SCREENING METHOD: A SCOPING REVIEW PROTOCOL
abstract: Introduction: Cervical cancer is a major global public health problem, even though it is largely preventable through Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, screening, and appropriate treatment of precursor lesions. The World Health Organization recommends HPV DNA testing as the primary screening method due to its higher sensitivity compared to cytology. Objective: to present the protocol for a scoping review aimed at mapping, characterizing, and describing the available evidence and recommendations regarding the use of HPV DNA molecular testing for cervical cancer screening. Method: The protocol will be conducted in accordance with the methodological recommendations of the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) and reported following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). The databases MEDLINE (through PubMed), Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, LILACS, and SciELO will be consulted, alongside gray literature sources from key national and international organizations and institutions. An exploratory search was conducted in MEDLINE (through PubMed) to identify indexing terms and keywords to inform the development of the search strategy, which will be adapted for the other databases. Retrieved records will be evaluated by two independent reviewers—initially through the screening of titles and abstracts, and subsequently through full-text review—based on eligibility criteria. Data will be extracted using a standardized instrument and synthesized in a descriptive and narrative manner. The process of identifying, selecting, and including records will be presented in a flowchart, in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Final thoughts: The review is expected to gather and characterize evidence and recommendations regarding the use of HPV DNA molecular testing for cervical cancer screening, covering screening strategies, management based on results, implementation aspects, areas of convergence and divergence, and knowledge gaps. The findings will inform the subsequent stages of the research and the development of a practical guide for Community Health Agents.

title: Improving coverage of cervical cancer screening for hard-to-reach women: lessons learned from piloting an innovative home-based screening model in Odisha, India
abstract: Cervical cancer is the second most common cancer among women in India, with mortality largely attributed to late-stage diagnosis and low screening coverage. Despite national efforts, screening uptake remains under 2% as reported in National Family Health Survey 5. This study assessed the feasibility and acceptability of a home-based HPV-DNA self-sampling model piloted in an underserved urban slum in Odisha, India. The screen–triage–treat model was implemented through the public health system in Thoria Sahi, Cuttack, targeting women aged 30–65 years. Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs) mobilized eligible women for home-based HPV-DNA self-sample collection. Women who tested positive were referred to Urban Primary Health Centres (UPHCs) for VIA-based triage. Those eligible received immediate thermal ablation, while others were referred for colposcopy, biopsy, and further management as per national guidelines at designated treatment centres. Data from October 2022 to September 2023 were analyzed to assess screening coverage, HPV positivity, follow-up, and treatment outcomes. Of 6,436 eligible women, 4,896 (76%) were screened. Among them, 322 (7%) tested positive for high-risk HPV. Despite counselling, only 42% (135/322) of HPV-positive women underwent VIA triage at UPHCs and of them 38.5% were found VIA-positive. Among VIA-positive women, 81% received thermal ablation, while the remainder were referred for colposcopy and biopsy and further management. Seven cases with pre-cancerous lesions and one case of micro-invasive carcinoma were diagnosed and managed appropriately. Community-based follow-up by ASHAs confirmed treatment adherence and well-being. Home-based HPV-DNA self-sampling integrated with existing public health infrastructure is a feasible and acceptable strategy to improve cervical cancer screening in low-resource urban settings. The model demonstrated strong community uptake and early lesion detection. Strengthening referral and treatment systems from the outset will be critical to achieving broader impact and scale.

title: Site-Specific Trends in Tumor Distribution, Treatment Patterns, and Survival in Head and Neck Cancer: A SEER Database Analysis
abstract: Abstract Head and neck cancer (HNC) management has evolved significantly with the introduction of organ-preservation protocols and changing disease etiology. To analyze site-specific trends in tumor distribution, staging, treatment modality, and survival outcomes using the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) program. A retrospective analysis of 288,132 malignant HNC cases from the SEER program (2000–2021) was performed. Survival analyses were restricted to cases diagnosed between 2000 and 2015 to allow for adequate follow-up. The anatomical sites included the salivary gland, larynx, the oral cavity, the lip, the tongue, the nasopharynx, the oropharynx, and the hypopharynx. Trends in tumor proportion, clinical stage, and treatment modality were assessed using linear regression. Five-year survival trends were analyzed using multivariate logistic regression. The proportion of tongue-cancer diagnoses increased by 12.2% (p < 0.001), while that of laryngeal cancer decreased by 10.0% (p < 0.001). Treatment patterns shifted significantly, with the rates of surgery combined with radiation (−11.0%; p < 0.001) and radiation alone (−7.6%; p < 0.001) declining, while that of chemoradiation increased (+16.9%; p < 0.001). The 5-year survival rates improved for hypopharynx (8.5%; p < 0.001), tongue (8.5%; p < 0.001), and oropharynx (8.0%; p < 0.01) cancers. The management of HNC has shifted toward multimodal therapies involving chemotherapy, coinciding with improved survival in pharyngeal and oral subsites. The rising proportion of tongue and oropharyngeal cases may reflect changes in underlying etiologic factors, including human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated disease, although HPV-specific effects cannot be directly assessed in the SEER program.

title: Cervical Cancer Burden in Africa: An Integrative Review of Epidemiology, Plant Medicine, and AI-Driven Innovation
abstract: Cervical cancer imposes a heavy burden in low- and middle-income countries and persistently high incidence and mortality in Sub-Saharan Africa due to unequal access to prevention and care. Although human papillomavirus (HPV) is a major driving factor, the risk is amplified by HIV co-infection, socioeconomic barriers, limited infrastructure, low health literacy, and behavioral factors, leading to frequent late-stage diagnosis, low screening coverage, and poor survival. Recent expansion of HPV vaccination programs since 2019 has achieved high coverage in some countries, but continent-wide rates remain below targets amid hesitancy, inequities, and systemic weaknesses. Thus, there is a critical need for an integrated synthesis of multidisciplinary evidence that reflects the peculiarities and diversities of African health systems. Moreover, high mortality rates underscore the need for integrated, context-specific evidence to strengthen vaccination, screening, and management strategies in line with WHO global elimination targets. Plant medicine promises to complement mainstream health delivery in low resource settings. Emerging artificial intelligence (AI) tools show strong potential to improve screening accuracy, reduce subjectivity and resource needs, and enhance early detection in resource-limited settings. This review synthesizes multidisciplinary data on economic impact, epidemiology, risk factors, prevention, diagnostic challenges, plant medicine and AI innovations to guide equitable progress in diverse African contexts.

title: Factors Associated with Self-Reported Previous HPV Testing Among Women Attending a Primary Healthcare Facility in Istanbul, Türkiye: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to estimate the proportion of women attending a primary healthcare facility in Istanbul, Türkiye, who reported previous human papillomavirus (HPV) testing and to examine associated factors, particularly depressive symptoms. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 507 women aged ≥18 years attending a Healthy Life Center in 2025. Sociodemographic characteristics, reproductive history, awareness of HPV testing availability and depressive symptoms (Beck Depression Inventory, BDI; total score 0–63) were recorded in face-to-face interviews. Two multivariable logistic regression models, without (Model A) and with (Model B) awareness, were fitted in the 441 women aged 30–65. Results: Of these women, 239 (54.2%) reported previous testing. In Model B, previous testing was associated with age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.07 per year; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.04–1.11) and awareness (aOR = 21.35; 95% CI: 8.07–56.51). A history of pregnancy loss or curettage was also associated with previous testing, but this finding was considered exploratory. The BDI total score was not clearly associated with previous testing in either model (Model B aOR = 0.99 per point; 95% CI: 0.97–1.01). Conclusions: Awareness was strongly associated with previous testing, but because both were reported at the same interview, the direction of this association is unknown, and no effect of awareness-raising can be inferred. No clear association was found with depressive symptoms, although a modest association cannot be excluded. These clinic-based, self-reported data do not reflect population screening coverage.

title: Integrated Microfluidic CRISPR-Based Diagnostic Device for Rapid Testing of HPVs
abstract: Screening for high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) is a pivotal strategy for the prevention of invasive cervical cancer, particularly in resource-constrained settings. In this study, we developed a CRISPR-based compact automated real-time detection system, termed Ccard, for rapid testing of HPV16, HPV18, and the internal reference gene GAPDH through a streamlined workflow. A simple room-temperature treatment efficiently releases nucleic acids directly from swab samples, bypassing the need for extraction. The mixture was driven through the channels and loaded into the reaction chambers on the microfluidic chip by a vacuum pump. The lyophilized reagents in the reaction zone of the microfluidic chip were redissolved. The system subsequently performs a single-step RPA-CRISPR/Cas13a reaction, with real-time detection enabled by an Internet of Things device. The assay achieved detection within 30 min, with a limit of detection (LOD) of 5 copies/μL for both HPV16 and HPV18. Validation with clinical samples demonstrated high sensitivity (96.8% for HPV16 and 100% for HPV18) and 100% specificity. These results highlight the reliability, precision, and strong potential of the Ccard system for rapid testing of HR-HPVs.

title: HPV prevalence among women in India from 2005 to 2026 and its relevance to vaccination and cervical cancer prevention: a meta-analysis (retrospective registration of methods as conducted)
abstract: This project contains the data, analysis code, and retrospective registration for a meta-analysis of human papillomavirus (HPV) prevalence among women in India, covering studies published from 1 January 2005 to 26 September 2026. Purpose: India introduced nationwide HPV vaccination in February 2026. Planning and monitoring the programme requires a clear picture of HPV infection among women before vaccine effects appear. Indian prevalence studies differ widely in population, recruitment setting, specimen, laboratory assay and endpoint definition, and earlier syntheses have often combined endpoints that measure different things. This review estimates three endpoints separately: any HPV detected by a broad assay, high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) detected by a broad high-risk panel, and HPV16/18, the types targeted by vaccination. It also examines how recruitment setting, risk of bias and assay relate to the estimates. The aim is to describe the available evidence and identify surveillance gaps, not to produce a national prevalence estimate or to measure vaccine impact. Methods: A PubMed-centered search with citation review identified 42 publications contributing 47 sample records. Prevalence was pooled separately for each endpoint using random-effects models on the logit scale (REML), with Hartung–Knapp intervals, prediction intervals, exploratory subgroup analyses and meta-regression, small-study tests, and sensitivity analyses for influential, small, high-risk-of-bias, and same-publication samples. Analyses were run in Stata 19.

title: Potential Benefit of Effective Implementation of Timely Postoperative Radiation for Head and Neck Cancer.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the potential benefit of survival of receiving timely postoperative radiation therapy (PORT) for head and neck cancer. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort. SETTING: National Cancer Database from 2004 to 2020. METHODS: Patients with a diagnosis of human papilloma virus (HPV)-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma who received adjuvant radiation were included. Exposure groups included timely PORT or delayed PORT (≤42 or >42 days from surgery to radiotherapy, respectively). The primary outcome was 5-year overall survival (OS). Inverse probability weighted models were used to estimate OS in the counter-factual scenario that all patients started radiation within 6 weeks while adjusting for confounding. Observed OS was for the entire cohort, while predicted OS was for the generated model of universal timely PORT within 6 weeks. Survival analyses were replicated for demographic and clinical subgroups. RESULTS: In total, 58,184 patients were included. Patients were mostly male, white, and non-Hispanic. The observed average 5-year OS was similar to the predicted OS (observed 0.58, 95% CI: 0.57-0.578; predicted 0.58, 95% CI: 0.57-0.59). The largest predicted benefit for timely PORT was seen in privately insured, white, rural, males, and with hypopharyngeal and stage IV cancer, though confidence intervals included the null hypothesis. Conversely, black patients were predicted to have a decline in OS with timely PORT (observed 0.54, 95% CI 0.53-0.56; predicted 0.50, 95% CI 0.46-0.52). CONCLUSION: For the overall cohort and other subgroups, even if optimally implemented, timely PORT is not predicted to improve OS. Modeling outcomes can guide resource allocation to the most impactful interventions.

source_records.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the potential benefit of survival of receiving timely postoperative radiation therapy (PORT) for head and neck cancer. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort. SETTING: National Cancer Database from 2004 to 2020. METHODS: Patients with a diagnosis of human papilloma virus (HPV)-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma who received adjuvant radiation were included. Exposure groups included timely PORT or delayed PORT (≤42 or >42 days from surgery to radiotherapy, respectively). The primary outcome was 5-year overall survival (OS). Inverse probability weighted models were used to estimate OS in the counter-factual scenario that all patients started radiation within 6 weeks while adjusting for confounding. Observed OS was for the entire cohort, while predicted OS was for the generated model of universal timely PORT within 6 weeks. Survival analyses were replicated for demographic and clinical subgroups. RESULTS: In total, 58,184 patients were included. Patients were mostly male, white, and non-Hispanic. The observed average 5-year OS was similar to the predicted OS (observed 0.58, 95% CI: 0.57-0.578; predicted 0.58, 95% CI: 0.57-0.59). The largest predicted benefit for timely PORT was seen in privately insured, white, rural, males, and with hypopharyngeal and stage IV cancer, though confidence intervals included the null hypothesis. Conversely, black patients were predicted to have a decline in OS with timely PORT (observed 0.54, 95% CI 0.53-0.56; predicted 0.50, 95% CI 0.46-0.52). CONCLUSION: For the overall cohort and other subgroups, even if optimally implemented, timely PORT is not predicted to improve OS. Modeling outcomes can guide resource allocation to the most impactful interventions.

title: Neurofibromatosis type 2 diagnosed at time of cervical squamous cell carcinoma
abstract: Introduction: Cervical cancer is most frequently diagnosed in women between ages 35–44 and rarely develops in younger women. Over 90% of cervical cancers are associated with human papillomavirus (HPV) persistence, but some are associated with genetic mutations such as STK11. This case discusses development of squamous cell carcinoma in a 25-year-old patient following low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL), cannot exclude high grade cytology result four years prior. Case Report: A 25-year-old G2P2 presented for a postpartum exam, which was notable for a 1 cm lesion of the anterior cervix. Biopsies confirmed squamous cell carcinoma. A positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) was completed for surgical planning which noted bilateral brain masses, concerning for vestibular schwannomas, which met clinical criteria for neurofibromatosis type 2 (NF2). Following referral to neurosurgery, a left retrosigmoid craniotomy was completed. A modified radical abdominal hysterectomy and sentinel lymph node dissection was performed following recovery from neurosurgery. Somatic genetic testing returned with a frameshift mutation in NF2E1194FJ. Final hysterectomy pathology noted a grade 3 tumor measuring 1.2 cm in size and with 3.75 mm depth of invasion. Conclusion: Low-grade intraepithelial lesion cytology typically has a high probability of regression and low risk for progression to cancer. Neurofibromin 2 regulates many cellular events. Studies note aberrant expression of NF2 contributes to tumorigenesis in other cancers. The tumorigenesis of both HPV and NF2 may share synergistic mechanisms which lead to progression to carcinoma. While the clinical course of our patient exhibits both a clinical diagnosis of NF2 and somatic NF2 loss in her cervical tumor, we cannot definitively conclude that NF2 deficiency accelerated the timeline of her cervical carcinogenesis. Rather, this clinical scenario prompts an intriguing hypothesis regarding potential molecular synergy between high-risk HPV oncoproteins and loss of the NF2 gene product, Merlin.

title: Multimodal Detection of a Minute Uterine Cornual Lesion in Cervical Clear Cell Carcinoma
abstract: Cervical clear cell carcinoma (CCC) is a rare human papillomavirus (HPV)-independent adenocarcinoma. A 73-year-old woman presented with postmenopausal bleeding. Ultrasonography demonstrated a cervical mass and a 5.0 × 5.0 mm right cornual nodule. On 3.0-T magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), the cornual lesion measured 5.2 × 5.3 mm and, like the cervical tumor, showed high signal intensity on diffusion-weighted imaging (b = 1000 s/mm2). 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) demonstrated intense uptake in the cervical mass (30.6 × 29.2 × 41.2 mm; SUVmax 10.4) and in the spatially separate right cornual nodule (5.2 × 5.1 mm; SUVmax 14.6), without FDG-avid nodal or distant metastatic disease. The concordant identification of the cornual lesion by ultrasonography, MRI, and PET/CT prompted multidisciplinary reassessment and radical hysterectomy to obtain definitive pathological characterization of both lesions. Histopathology demonstrated clear cell carcinoma at both sites; however, because molecular, genomic, or clonality analyses were not performed, their biological relationship remains uncertain. All 30 examined lymph nodes and the surgical margins were negative. The cervical primary was staged as pT1b3 pN0 cM0 (FIGO 2018 stage IB3). The patient received four cycles of postoperative chemotherapy with paclitaxel plus cisplatin. At 14 months after surgery, gynecological examination and pelvic MRI showed no evidence of recurrence. This case highlights the complementary roles of ultrasonography, MRI, and 18F-FDG PET/CT in characterizing a minute spatially separate uterine lesion while underscoring the need for cautious interpretation when the relationship between lesions cannot be established.

title: Spatial lipidomics in gynecologic malignancies: molecular identification, cellular attribution, and mechanistic validation
abstract: Spatial lipidomics can place lipid identities within histopathologic compartments, but ion maps are frequently interpreted beyond what their analytical and biological validation can support. Here, we critically synthesize direct spatial lipid evidence in ovarian, endometrial, and cervical cancers and use spatial metabolomics, mass spectrometry imaging, spatial transcriptomics or proteomics, and non-spatial lipid biology only as explicitly graded support. We organize inference as an eight-gate chain: pathology-defined sampling, analytical quality control, structural identification, cellular attribution, metabolic flux, perturbation and rescue, patient-level validation, and prospective clinical utility. Within this framework, lipid uptake, de novo synthesis, desaturation, fatty-acid oxidation, membrane remodeling, prostaglandin E2 signaling, and ferroptosis are interpreted as mechanistic programs downstream of spatially anchored observations. Disease ecology determines which programs are plausible: omental adipocyte-tumor exchange dominates ovarian cancer, obesity-estrogen-insulin and PI3K signaling frame endometrial cancer, and persistent high-risk human papillomavirus infection shapes membrane and inflammatory remodeling in cervical cancer. Evidence remains highly asymmetric. Ovarian cancer has the broadest spatial literature; endometrial evidence relies principally on one 64-patient DESI-MSI cohort; and cervical evidence is limited to very small phospholipid and oleate studies. Spatial lipidomics is therefore ready to localize disease-specific niches, prioritize causal experiments, and define testable patient subsets, but not yet to support routine screening, diagnosis, treatment selection, or surveillance. Closing the gap requires orthogonal structural confirmation, cell-resolved source assignment, isotope tracing, functional rescue, and locked multicenter validation.

title: KNOWLEDGE OF CERVICAL CANCER AND HPV, ATTITUDES TOWARD HPV VACCINATION, AND RECOMMENDATION PRACTICES AMONG PRIMARY HEALTHCARE WORKERS: A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Cervical cancer (CC) is largely preventable through screening and human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination; successful prevention depends on effective implementation of these interventions in primary care. We evaluated primary healthcare workers’ knowledge, awareness, attitudes, and self-reported behaviors regarding CC, HPV, and HPV vaccination.MATERIAL AND METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, data were collected using face-to-face questionnaires from 305 healthcare workers at Family Health Centers and Community Health Centers in Afyonkarahisar, Türkiye, between February 15 and June 15, 2023. Analyses were performed using IBM SPSS Statistics 26.0. Categorical variables were compared using chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests. Multivariable logistic regression assessed factors associated with HPV vaccine recommendation and willingness to vaccinate one’s child. Statistical significance was defined as p<0.05.RESULTS: Although 86.2% stated that CC is preventable, only 45.2% identified HPV infection as the most important risk factor. Awareness that HPV can cause CC (92.8%) and is sexually transmitted (97.4%) was high, whereas knowledge of its natural course was limited. Self-reported personal vaccination rates were low (bivalent 3.3%; quadrivalent 10.8%). Overall, 65.2% (n=199) recommended HPV vaccination to patients, 79.3% (n=242) were willing to vaccinate their child, and 66.9% (n=204) reported having knowledge of HPV vaccines. Compared with other healthcare workers, physicians had higher odds of recommending vaccination (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.20, 95% CI 1.63–6.29). Education on CC, its treatment, and screening during professional training was associated with higher adjusted odds of recommending vaccination (aOR 3.60, 95% CI 2.11–6.13) and willingness to vaccinate one’s child (aOR 3.11, 95% CI 1.71–5.65).CONCLUSIONS: Primary healthcare workers showed item-specific gaps in knowledge of CC, HPV, and HPV vaccination, alongside low self-reported personal vaccination rates. Strengthening structured education in primary care may support HPV vaccine counseling and recommendation practices.

title: Diagnostic uncertainty in a patient with severe hidradenitis suppurativa revealing Buschke-Löwenstein tumor.
abstract: Buschke-Löwenstein tumor (BLT), also known as giant condyloma acuminatum, is a rare human papillomavirus-associated lesion characterized by locally aggressive growth with the potential for malignant transformation. Diagnosis may be particularly challenging when BLT arises in the setting of severe chronic inflammatory disease. We present a 44-year-old man with severe hidradenitis suppurativa, well-controlled HIV infection, recurrent gluteal abscesses, and chronic sacral osteomyelitis who presented with worsening perineal pain and chronic drainage. Although imaging demonstrated extensive infiltrative soft-tissue disease suspicious for neoplasm with superimposed infection, the patient's severe chronic inflammatory disease, recurrent abscesses, and chronic osteomyelitis created substantial diagnostic uncertainty. After the patient did not improve with broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy, open biopsy of a large fungating perianal lesion established the diagnosis of BLT. This case highlights the diagnostic uncertainty that may arise when BLT coexists with severe hidradenitis suppurativa, emphasizing the importance of early tissue biopsy when clinical features are atypical or progressive.

title: Pediatric conjunctival papilloma managed with staged multimodal therapy: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Conjunctival papilloma is a rare benign ocular surface tumor in children, most commonly associated with low-risk human papillomavirus types 6 and 11. Management can be challenging because of multifocal disease, persistence, recurrence, and the need to preserve healthy conjunctival tissue in young patients. We report a pediatric case of multifocal conjunctival papilloma successfully managed with a staged multimodal approach combining preoperative medical therapy with limited surgical excision. CASE PRESENTATION: A 4-year-old boy presented with multifocal conjunctival papillomatous lesions. Following clinical evaluation and diagnosis of conjunctival papilloma, preoperative topical and intralesional interferon alfa-2b were administered to reduce the lesion size. Residual lesions were subsequently treated with limited surgical excision following preoperative interferon-mediated debulking and intraoperative application of mitomycin C. The patient had a favorable clinical course, with preservation and progressive restoration of the conjunctival architecture. At 2 years of follow-up, there was no evidence of recurrence. CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the potential value of a staged multimodal strategy for managing multifocal conjunctival papilloma in children. Preoperative medical debulking followed by targeted surgical excision may help reduce the extent of surgery, preserve healthy conjunctival tissue, and achieve durable disease control. This approach may be particularly useful in pediatric ocular surface disease, where tissue preservation is an important consideration.

title: Postoperative ctDNA could potentially spare patients from unnecessary adjuvant therapy in HPV-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a meta-analysis
abstract: Background The prognostic utility of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) for minimal residual disease detection in human papillomavirus (HPV)-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) remains incompletely characterized. This meta-analysis evaluates the association between post-operative ctDNA and recurrence-free survival (RFS) in this population. Methods A systematic search of major databases through May 2026 identified studies evaluating post-operative ctDNA and RFS in HPV-negative HNSCC. title: Written in Blood: Liquid Biopsies for Cervical Cancer Screening
abstract: Cervical cancer (CC) is one of the most common malignancies affecting women across the world. The major cause of CC is human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. Studies have shown that HPV infection is highly correlated (>99%) with the occurrence of CC. HPV testing is done on women infected with high-risk HPV types that correlate strongly to CC development, such as HPV types 16 and 18. In conjunction with HPV testing, traditional CC screening (Pap test and visual inspection test) is done as standard practice against all HPV types. However, the Pap test and HPV testing are highly invasive techniques that require collection of cervical cells at annual intervals for at-risk women. In addition, such tests pose significant socio-economic challenges, especially in countries where the combination of inadequate infrastructure and inadequate medical expertise greatly reduce test accuracy. Recently, liquid biopsy has been extensively examined as an alternative to cancer screening and diagnostics. Liquid biopsy is a non-invasive technique that screens for circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and circulating tumor cells (CTC) in the blood. ctDNA are fragments of cell-free DNA, shed from cell death, that contain hallmark mutations of cancerous cells. CTCs are tumor cells that have metastasized from primary tumor sites and are released into the bloodstream. Due to advances in high-throughput sequencing, the analysis of CTC and ctDNA is possible. Liquid biopsies can also detect real-time molecular changes that occur in the cancer and provide a more complete tumor profile regarding the number of tumor DNA mutations. Liquid biopsy provides an exciting alternative for patients who may be unwilling to undergo invasive, and often painful, CC and HPV screening. Furthermore, it may greatly reduce medical costs as no specialized training is required to obtain samples, and it allows health-care practitioners to perform more testing, effectively monitoring disease progression. This can enable more targeted approaches to CC treatment and dramatically improve patient outcomes.

title: HPV Related Multiphenotypic Sinonasal Carcinoma: An Emerging Pathologic Entity
abstract: Human papillomavirus-related multiphenotypic sinonasal carcinoma (HMSC) is a recently recognised, uncommon malignancy of the sinonasal tract characterised by a distinctive biphasic morphology and consistent association with high-risk HPV types, most often HPV-33. Although histologically high-grade, HMSC paradoxically demonstrates a relatively indolent clinical course, making accurate diagnosis crucial to avoid overtreatment. We report the case of a 42-year-old female who presented with unilateral epiphora and a painful, firm left-sided facial swelling of five months’ duration. This case reinforces the importance of recognising the characteristic morphology and immunophenotype of HMSC. Increased awareness of this emerging entity is essential to ensure appropriate diagnostic classification and optimal clinical management.
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Knowledge attitudes and practices regarding cervical cancer and its prevention among women of reproductive age living in urban slums of Eastern India
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major public health problem in developing countries, particularly among women residing in urban slums where awareness and access to preventive services are limited. The objective of the study was to assess knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding cervical cancer and its prevention among women of reproductive age residing in urban slums of Bhubaneswar, India. A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 138 women aged 15–49 years residing in urban slums of Bhubaneswar, India between November, 2024 and March, 2025. Data were collected using a pretested semi-structured questionnaire assessing knowledge, attitudes, and practices related to cervical cancer and its prevention. Only 6.5% participants had heard about cervical cancer, and 4.3% were aware of its risk factors. Knowledge regarding symptoms (3.6%), screening (2.2%), and Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination (0.7%) was extremely low. All participants were presented with the knowledge items, with a “Don’t know” response available for participants who were unfamiliar with the topic; therefore, the reported percentages for individual knowledge items reflect responses from the full study sample rather than only those who had previously heard of cervical cancer. Despite poor knowledge, attitudes were relatively positive, with 64.5% strongly agreeing that discussion of cervical cancer is important and 71% willing to undergo screening if it were provided free of charge. Screening practice was poor, with only 0.7% reporting that they had ever undergone a Pap smear test. Lack of awareness was reported as the major barrier (98.6%). The findings demonstrate a substantial knowledge-practice gap despite relatively favourable attitudes towards cervical cancer prevention. Context-specific health education, strengthened engagement of healthcare providers, and improved access to cervical cancer screening and HPV vaccination services are needed, particularly in underserved urban-slum population.

title: Perception of virus effects and vaccination among people with multiple sclerosis in Saudi Arabia
abstract: Background People with multiple sclerosis (pwMS) are at increased risk of infection due to immune dysregulation and exposure to disease-modifying therapies (DMTs). Despite this risk, real-world vaccine uptake remains inconsistent. This study evaluated vaccination readiness, counseling practices, and infection-related perceptions among pwMS in Saudi Arabia. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted among adults with MS ( n = 204) recruited using non-probability (convenience) sampling from tertiary-care clinical and community-based sources. The survey assessed demographic characteristics, vaccination attitudes and uptake, counseling experiences, perceptions of infection risk related to MS and DMTs, and awareness of Epstein–Barr virus (EBV). Internal consistency of multi-item measures was acceptable (Cronbach's α = 0.72). Descriptive statistics were used to summarize outcomes. title: Ultrasensitive and Specific Detection of Neutralization-Correlated Serum Antibodies Via Secondary Antibody−DNA Linker-Mediated Magnetic Bead−Based Proximity Extension Assay
abstract: Abstract Sensitive, accurate, and readily deployable detection of neutralizing antibody (NAb) titers is essential for evaluating vaccine efficacy and population-level immunity. Here, we report an Antibody-DNA Linker (AND Linker) comprising a fusion of Protein A/G, a G4S flexible peptide, and duck circovirus replication initiator protein (DCV). This design enables orthogonal, site-specific assembly: the N-terminal Protein A/G binds the IgG Fc region, while the C-terminal DCV covalently captures 5′ ssDNA at a defined 1:1 molar ratio. Unlike random chemical crosslinking, which suffers from heterogeneous attachment sites, variable stoichiometry, and poor reproducibility, the AND Linker ensures uniform functional orientation and minimal batch-to-batch variation. By optimizing ssDNA secondary structure, we further enhanced DCV recognition efficiency. Integrating this linker into a magnetic bead-based proximity extension assay (termed SADL-MPEA), we achieved femtomolar-level detection of serum antibodies highly correlated with neutralizing activity. For HPV16 and HPV18, SADL-MPEA demonstrated limits of detection (LOD) approximately three orders of magnitude lower than conventional PEA using random chemical conjugation. In clinical serum validation against the pseudovirus neutralization test (PBNT), SADL-MPEA showed strong concordance (Pearson’s r = 0.84−0.85), confirming its utility as a reliable surrogate for functional neutralization capacity. Diagnostic performance was exceptional, with sensitivities of 90.9% (HPV16) and 83.3% (HPV18), 100% specificity for both, and an area under the ROC curve of 0.99. Crucially, SADL-MPEA requires only antigen-coated magnetic beads to adapt to new targets, as the DNA-labeled secondary antibody remains universal. This platform offers a simple, high-throughput, and scalable solution for NAb-correlated antibody detection in research and clinical settings.
